title: Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve-in-Valve Implantation for the Treatment of Dysfunctional Surgical Bioprosthetic Valves: An International, Multicenter Registry Study.
journal: Circulation

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre registry; 156 patients with bioprosthetic TV dysfunction.
appraisal.main_limitation: Uncontrolled, heterogeneous registry with a young median age (40 years) and a median follow-up of 13.3 months.
appraisal.one_line: International registry of transcatheter valve-in-valve implantation within failed surgical tricuspid bioprostheses.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Among 152 patients in whom TVIV was attempted with a Melody (n=94) or Sapien (n=58) valve, implantation was successful in 150, with few serious complications.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Largest series supporting tricuspid valve-in-valve as an alternative to reoperation.

title: Surgery Does Not Improve Survival in Patients With Isolated Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective analysis of 3,276 adults with isolated severe TR, of whom 171 (5%) underwent tricuspid valve surgery.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective single-database design with few surgical patients and a wide confidence interval.
appraisal.one_line: Echocardiography-database cohort finding no survival difference with surgery for isolated severe tricuspid regurgitation after immortal time adjustment.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: When considering surgery as a time-dependent covariate in a propensity-matched sample, there was no difference in overall survival between patients who received medical versus surgical therapy (hazard ratio: 1.34; 95% confidence interval: 0.78 to 2.30; p = 0.288).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Bears on the timing and benefit of tricuspid intervention.

title: 3-Year Outcomes After Valve-in-Valve Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement for Degenerated Bioprostheses: The PARTNER 2 Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective multicenter PARTNER 2 registries of 365 high-risk patients undergoing valve-in-valve procedures.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm registry without a comparator.
appraisal.one_line: Three-year outcomes of valve-in-valve TAVR for degenerated surgical bioprostheses in the PARTNER 2 registry.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 3 years, the overall Kaplan-Meier estimate of all-cause mortality was 32.7%. Aortic valve re-replacement was required in 1.9%.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports durability of valve-in-valve TAVR in high-risk patients.

title: Transcatheter Versus Medical Treatment of Patients With Symptomatic Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry-based propensity-matched case-control study; 472 TTVI patients and 1,179 medically managed controls, 268 matched pairs.
appraisal.main_limitation: Matching on only three variables with retrospective controls, so residual confounding and selection are likely.
appraisal.one_line: TriValve propensity-matched registry comparison associated transcatheter tricuspid intervention with lower 1-year mortality and heart failure rehospitalisation than medical therapy.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with control subjects, TTVI patients had lower 1-year mortality (23 ± 3% vs. 36 ± 3%; p = 0.001), rehospitalization (26 ± 3% vs. 47 ± 3%; p < 0.0001), and composite endpoint (32 ± 4% vs. 49 ± 3%; p = 0.0003).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Gives early comparative signal for T-TEER and TTVR where randomised evidence is lacking.

title: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for reduction of tricuspid regurgitation: 6-month outcomes of the TRILUMINATE single-arm study.
journal: Lancet (London, England)

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective, multicentre, single-arm study at 21 sites in Europe and the USA, 85 patients enrolled and underwent successful TriClip implantation.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm design without a control group and with short follow-up.
appraisal.one_line: Single-arm study of TriClip transcatheter edge-to-edge repair showing reduction in tricuspid regurgitation against prespecified performance goals.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Tricuspid regurgitation severity was reduced by at least one grade at 30 days in 71 (86%) of 83 patients who had available echocardiogram data and imaging. At 6 months, three (4%) of 84 patients experienced a major adverse event, which was less than the prespecified performance goal of 39% (p<0·0001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Early device evidence for T-TEER in a condition with few treatment options, informing the need for randomised trials.

title: 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease: Executive Summary: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
journal: Circulation

appraisal.design_and_n: Guideline executive summary; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Many recommendations rest on lower levels of evidence; the abstract gives no class or level detail.
appraisal.one_line: 2020 ACC/AHA valvular heart disease guideline executive summary, including timing and choice of surgical and catheter interventions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Primary US reference for TAVI, mitral and tricuspid intervention decisions, to compare with ESC guidance.

title: 2020 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Valvular Heart Disease: Executive Summary: A Report of the American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Joint Committee on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Guideline executive summary; no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: Same document as the Circulation publication; recommendation levels not given in the abstract.
appraisal.one_line: 2020 ACC/AHA valvular heart disease guideline executive summary (JACC publication), covering diagnostic work-up and timing and choice of interventions.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Primary US reference for valve intervention decisions; duplicate publication of the same guideline.

title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Treatment of Tricuspid Regurgitation.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: TRILUMINATE (NCT03227757), prospective single-arm multicentre study, n = 85.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm, without a control group and with core-laboratory echocardiographic surrogate endpoints.
appraisal.one_line: One-year outcomes of the single-arm TRILUMINATE study showed durable TR reduction and clinical improvement after tricuspid TEER.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, TR was reduced to moderate or less in 71% of subjects compared with 8% at baseline (p < 0.0001). The overall major adverse event rate and all-cause mortality were both 7.1% at 1 year.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Early device evidence for T-TEER that preceded randomised comparison.

title: Concomitant Tricuspid Repair in Patients with Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial, 401 patients undergoing mitral-valve surgery for degenerative mitral regurgitation.
appraisal.main_limitation: The benefit was driven by progression of tricuspid regurgitation rather than clinical outcomes, and follow-up was 2 years.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial found that adding tricuspid annuloplasty to mitral surgery reduced a composite of tricuspid events at 2 years, with more pacemaker implantation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary event rate was 3.9% vs. 10.2% (relative risk, 0.37; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.16 to 0.86; P = 0.02). Permanent pacemaker implantation was 14.1% vs. 2.5% (rate ratio, 5.75; 95% CI, 2.27 to 14.60).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs timing of tricuspid intervention and the surgical comparator for transcatheter tricuspid and mitral therapies.

title: Factors influencing post-surgical survival in degenerative mitral regurgitation.
journal: European heart journal

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 2276 patients undergoing mitral valve surgery across five centres; 278 patients (12.2%) died over median follow-up of 5.6 (3.6 to 8.7) years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry data from five centres with residual confounding possible; the abstract does not describe transcatheter alternatives.
appraisal.one_line: Registry cohort relating the number of secondary outcome determinants to survival after surgery for degenerative mitral regurgitation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Adjusted hazard ratios for post-operative all-cause mortality were 1.56 (95% CI: 1.11-2.20), 1.78 (95% CI: 1.23-2.58) and 2.58 (95% CI: 1.73-3.83) for one, two, and three or four secondary outcome determinants respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Supports earlier surgical referral thresholds and informs the choice between surgery and transcatheter repair in degenerative mitral regurgitation.

title: Transcatheter Repair for Patients with Tricuspid Regurgitation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial; 350 patients enrolled, 175 assigned to each group, mean age 78 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: The primary hierarchical endpoint appears driven by quality-of-life change, with no difference in hard components.
appraisal.one_line: Randomised trial of tricuspid TEER plus medical therapy versus medical therapy alone in severe tricuspid regurgitation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The results for the primary end point favored the TEER group (win ratio, 1.48; 95% confidence interval, 1.06 to 2.13; P = 0.02); the incidence of death or tricuspid-valve surgery and the rate of hospitalization for heart failure did not appear to differ between the groups.
appraisal.why_it_matters: First pivotal randomised evidence for transcatheter tricuspid repair, shaping guideline positions and coverage decisions.

title: 1-Year Outcomes of Transcatheter Tricuspid Valve Repair.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective, single-arm, multicentre early feasibility study, Sixty-five patients enrolled (mean age of 77.4 years; 55.4% female).
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm design without a control group and a small sample; echocardiographic data available in a subset at one year.
appraisal.one_line: One-year outcomes of the single-arm CLASP TR early feasibility study of the PASCAL system for tricuspid regurgitation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 30 days, cardiovascular mortality was 3.1% and the stroke rate was 1.5%. At one year, 31 of 36 (86.0%) patients achieved moderate or less TR; freedom from all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization by Kaplan-Meier analyses were 87.9% and 78.5%, respectively; 6-minute walk distance increased by 94 m (P = 0.014) and KCCQ scores improved by 18 points (P < 0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Early device-specific evidence for T-TEER supporting regulatory and guideline discussion, without comparative data.

title: Transfemoral tricuspid valve replacement and one-year outcomes: the TRISCEND study.
journal: European heart journal

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective, single-arm, multicentre study enrolling 176 patients with ≥moderate symptomatic TR.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm design without a control group; manufacturer-funded.
appraisal.one_line: One-year outcomes of the single-arm TRISCEND study of transfemoral EVOQUE tricuspid valve replacement.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Tricuspid regurgitation was reduced to ≤mild in 97.6% (P < .001). NYHA class I or II was achieved in 93.3% (P < .001), Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score increased by 25.7 points (P < .001), and six-minute walk distance increased by 56.2 m (P < .001). All-cause mortality was 9.1%, and 10.2% of patients were hospitalized for heart failure.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Key device evidence for TTVR ahead of comparative trial data.

title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair in COAPT-Ineligible Patients With Functional Mitral Regurgitation.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort of 6,675 patients who underwent MTEER for FMR; 3,721 (55.7%) trial-eligible and 2,954 (44.3%) trial-ineligible.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational registry with no non-TEER comparator among ineligible patients, so benefit cannot be estimated.
appraisal.one_line: TVT Registry analysis of outcomes of mitral TEER in functional MR patients who would have been ineligible for COAPT.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: There was a higher risk of 1-year death or HFH (HR: 1.73; 95% CI: 1.57-1.91; P < 0.001) in trial-ineligible patients. A clinically meaningful improvement in health status at 30 days was observed in 78.9% and 77.0% of patients in the trial-ineligible and trial-eligible groups, respectively.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shows nearly half of real-world patients lie outside the defining trial, a gap relevant to transportability work.

title: Real-World 1-Year Results of Tricuspid Edge-to-Edge Repair From the bRIGHT Study.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Prospective, single-arm, open-label, multicentre registry at 26 sites in Europe, n = 511 (NCT04483089).
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm registry without a control group and with manufacturer sponsorship.
appraisal.one_line: One-year results of the bRIGHT post-approval registry of TriClip tricuspid TEER.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: TR was reduced to moderate or less in 81% at 1 year. NYHA class I/II rose from 21% to 75% (P < 0.0001) and KCCQ improved by 19 ± 26 points (P <0.0001). Baseline serum creatinine and TAPSE were independently associated with mortality at 1 year (OR: 2.169; 95% CI: 1.494-3.147; P < 0.0001; OR: 0.636; 95% CI: 0.415-0.974; P = 0.0375).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Real-world durability data for T-TEER pending comparative trial results.

title: Benefit of isolated surgical valve repair or replacement for functional tricuspid regurgitation and long-term outcomes stratified by the TRI-SCORE.
journal: European heart journal

appraisal.design_and_n: Patients managed conservatively (one thousand and two hundred seventeen) and 551 who underwent isolated tricuspid valve surgery (200 repairs and 351 replacements), international cohort of 33 centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational comparison open to selection bias and confounding by indication, with surgical rather than transcatheter treatment.
appraisal.one_line: TRIGISTRY cohort suggests surgery for isolated functional tricuspid regurgitation improved survival only in patients with a low TRI-SCORE.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 10 years, survival rates were similar between surgical and conservative management [41% vs. 36%; hazard ratio (HR) .97; 95% confidence interval (CI) .88-1.08, P = .57]. Surgery improved survival compared with conservative management in the low TRI-SCORE category (72% vs. 44%; HR .27; 95% CI .20-.37, P < .0001), but not in the intermediate (36% vs. 37%; HR 1.17; 95%CI .98-1.40, P = .09) or high categories (20% vs. 24%; HR 1.06; 95% CI .91-1.25, P = .45).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs timing and patient selection for tricuspid intervention, including how transcatheter trials should stratify risk.

title: Transcatheter Valve Repair for Tricuspid Regurgitation: 1-Year Results From a Large European Real-World Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Multicentre retrospective and prospective observational cohort, 1,059 patients across 16 European centres.
appraisal.main_limitation: Single-arm observational design without a control group, with a mix of retrospective and prospective enrolment.
appraisal.one_line: Large European registry of PASCAL tricuspid transcatheter edge-to-edge repair with centrally analysed echocardiography to 1 year.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Intraprocedural success according to Tricuspid Valve Academic Research Consortium criteria was achieved in 85%, and TR reduced to ≤moderate in 87%. At 1 year, 83% of patients showed ≤moderate TR.
appraisal.why_it_matters: One of the largest real-world datasets on tricuspid TEER, informing patient selection and device generation effects.

title: Tricuspid Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation: 1-Year Outcomes From the TRILUMINATE Randomized Cohort.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized controlled trial; 572 subjects randomized.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label control comparison, with the composite driven by patient-reported outcomes rather than hard events.
appraisal.one_line: TRILUMINATE one-year outcomes in the full randomized cohort show a hierarchical composite benefit for T-TEER driven by quality of life, with no difference in death, surgery or heart failure hospitalisation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary endpoint was met for the full cohort (win ratio = 1.84; P < 0.0001). Annualized HFH rate was comparable between device and control subjects (0.17 vs 0.20 events/patient-year; P = 0.40).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Shapes the evidence for tricuspid TEER, where benefit on mortality and hospitalisation remains unproven.

title: Transcatheter Valve Replacement in Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized international trial; 400 patients, 2:1 allocation (267 valve replacement, 133 control).
appraisal.main_limitation: Industry-funded open-label trial with a composite driven by quality-of-life measures, and no mortality or hospitalisation advantage.
appraisal.one_line: TRISCEND II found transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement superior to medical therapy on a hierarchical composite driven by symptoms and quality of life, with more bleeding and pacemaker implantation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, the win ratio favoring valve replacement was 2.02 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.56 to 2.62; P<0.001). Severe bleeding occurred in 15.4% of the valve-replacement group and in 5.3% of the control group (P = 0.003); new permanent pacemakers were implanted in 17.4% and 2.3%, respectively (P<0.001).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Pivotal randomized evidence for transcatheter tricuspid replacement, with a clear safety trade-off.

title: Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Severe Isolated Tricuspid Regurgitation: The Tri.Fr Randomized Clinical Trial.
journal: JAMA

appraisal.design_and_n: Investigator-initiated randomized trial at 24 centers; 300 patients (152 T-TEER + OMT, 148 OMT alone).
appraisal.main_limitation: Composite is driven by patient-reported outcomes in an unblinded trial.
appraisal.one_line: Tri.Fr found T-TEER plus medical therapy improved a composite score driven by patient-reported outcomes in isolated severe tricuspid regurgitation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 1 year, 109 patients (74.1%) in the T-TEER + OMT group had an improved composite score compared with 58 patients (40.6%) in the OMT-alone group.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Independent randomized confirmation of T-TEER benefit for symptoms and quality of life.

title: Tricuspid regurgitation and outcomes in mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair.
journal: European heart journal

appraisal.design_and_n: Registry cohort in OCEAN-Mitral: 2103 (no TR), 201 (new-onset TR), 504 (normalized TR), and 858 (residual TR) patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Observational with echocardiographic grouping defined after the procedure, so landmark and confounding issues remain.
appraisal.one_line: OCEAN-Mitral registry analysis linking post-procedural tricuspid regurgitation, rather than baseline TR, to outcomes after mitral TEER.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Compared with no TR as a reference, hazard ratio 1.83 (95% confidence interval: 1.39-2.40) for new-onset TR, 1.45 (1.23-1.72) for residual TR, and 0.82 (0.65-1.04) for normalized TR for cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Suggests post-procedural TR status, not baseline TR, is the relevant prognostic marker for concomitant tricuspid treatment decisions in mitral TEER.

title: Two-Year Outcomes of Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Severe Tricuspid Regurgitation: The TRILUMINATE Pivotal Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: Circulation

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomized controlled trial; 572 patients.
appraisal.main_limitation: Crossover of control patients to device treatment limits the long-term comparison.
appraisal.one_line: Two-year TRILUMINATE data show fewer recurrent heart failure hospitalisations with tricuspid TEER and similar mortality.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The annualized rate of recurrent heart failure hospitalizations through 2 years was significantly lower with tricuspid TEER compared with control (0.19 event per patient-year versus 0.26 event per patient-year; P=0.02; joint frailty model hazard ratio, 0.72; one-sided upper confidence limit, 0.93; P=0.02).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Adds evidence on hard hospitalisation outcomes for tricuspid TEER.

title: Outcomes of Percutaneous Mechanical Aspiration in Right-Sided Infective Endocarditis: A Multicenter Registry.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Retrospective multicentre registry, 256 patients from 19 institutions.
appraisal.main_limitation: Retrospective, uncontrolled and based on site-reported vegetation size, so comparison with medical or surgical management is not possible.
appraisal.one_line: Multicentre registry of percutaneous mechanical aspiration for right-sided infective endocarditis reports high procedural success with substantial in-hospital events.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: Procedural success was achieved in 89.4%; the primary endpoint occurred in 18% (mortality: 9.8%; new PE: 8.3%; emergency surgery: 3.1%).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Largest series of this emerging catheter-based debulking approach, informing safety expectations before any randomised comparison.

title: Tricuspid valve replacement outcomes by baseline tricuspid regurgitation severity: the TRISCEND II trial.
journal: European heart journal

appraisal.design_and_n: Post hoc analysis of randomised trial, 400 patients (TTVR 267, control 133); severe TR n = 172, massive/torrential n = 220.
appraisal.main_limitation: Post hoc subgroup analysis, with wide intervals for mortality and heart failure hospitalisation differences.
appraisal.one_line: Post hoc TRISCEND II analysis suggests benefit of transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement across severe and massive/torrential baseline TR.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary safety and effectiveness endpoint (win ratio) favoured TTVR over control: severe 1.64 (95% CI: 1.11, 2.43) and massive/torrential 2.20 (1.55, 3.14).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Informs patient selection and timing of tricuspid valve replacement by baseline regurgitation severity.

title: Tricuspid-Valve Intervention in Heart Failure.
journal: The New England journal of medicine

appraisal.design_and_n: Randomised trial in heart failure; 360 patients (237 tricuspid repair, 123 medical therapy).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label design with a hierarchical composite including quality-of-life improvement.
appraisal.one_line: Transcatheter tricuspid repair plus medical therapy was superior to medical therapy alone for a hierarchical composite in symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The win ratio for the first primary end point was 2.42 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.76 to 3.33; P<0.001); hazard ratio for death from any cause or hospitalization for heart failure, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.29 to 0.55.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Randomised evidence of mortality or hospitalisation benefit for tricuspid intervention, informing timing and guideline class.

title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society/Canadian Society of Cardiovascular Surgery/Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology Clinical Practice Update on Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Valve Intervention: Patient Evaluation and Management.
journal: The Canadian journal of cardiology

appraisal.design_and_n: Clinical practice update from Canadian societies; the abstract gives no sample size.
appraisal.main_limitation: The abstract does not describe the evidence grading method.
appraisal.one_line: A Canadian clinical practice update on transcatheter mitral and tricuspid edge-to-edge repair and replacement.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The abstract does not report an effect estimate.
appraisal.why_it_matters: It offers contemporary referral and patient-selection guidance across mitral and tricuspid transcatheter therapy.
